title: webshot2 incompatibility with bookdown for PDF output

title: vwidth vheight not set before screenshotting html
description:
I have been using webshot2 in combination with htmlwidgets::saveWidget to screenshot DataTables and Leaflet objects for inclusion in a customisable Rmd document. 
I believe the recent chromote updates (mentioned in #72) have impacted webshot's ability to screenshot html files. I can obtain screenshots but the html does not get sized to fit the vwidth and vheight specified, although the png produced does have the correct dimensions, it it mostly empty whitespace with the html content in the top-left corner.

I have the most up to date versions of chromote, and webshot2 installed.

My reprex:
```
library(webshot2)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(DT)

data(mtcars)
datatable <- DT::datatable(mtcars)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(widget = datatable,
                        file = "./plot.html",
                        libdir = "./dependents")
# The html can be resized to whatever the size of the "window" it's in.
webshot2::webshot("./plot.html", file = "./plot.png",
                  delay = 5,
                vwidth = 1700,  # viewport width in pixels
                vheight = 850,
                cliprect = "viewport")
# I expect the generated png file to have the table filling the whole of the space (1700*850)
```

title: `expand` argument of `webshot()` not working as expected
description:
The documentation states that `expand` lets me add a fixed number of pixels to the clipping rectangle: 

> **expand** A numeric vector specifying how many pixels to expand the clipping rectangle by. If one number, the rectangle will be expanded by that many pixels on all sides. [...]
https://rstudio.github.io/webshot2/reference/webshot.html

In the following reprex `expand` seems to have no effect

```r
library(htmltools)

fn_html <- 'test.html'
fn_img <- 'test.png'
url <- paste0('file://', here::here(fn_html))

tags <- htmltools::tags

# -- setup html to capture: a 100x100px square box

tags$body(
  tags$div(style = "width: 100px; height: 100px; background-color: red"),
  style = "margin: 0;"   # chrome browser default is `margin: 8px`
) |> 
  as.character() |> 
  writeLines(con = file(fn_html))

# -- trying to get `expand` to work

webshot2::webshot(
  url = url,
  file = fn_img,
  vwidth = 100,     
  vheight = 100
)
utils::browseURL(fn_img)  # result: 100x100px (as expected)

webshot2::webshot(
  url = url,
  file = fn_img,
  vwidth = 100,     
  vheight = 100,
  expand = 200            # expectation: add 200px on each side
)
utils::browseURL(fn_img)  # result: 100x100px - expand has no effect on size

webshot2::webshot(
  url = url,
  file = fn_img,
  vwidth = 100,     
  vheight = 100,
  cliprect = c(0,0,50,50),
  expand = 200             # expectation: add 200px on each side
)
utils::browseURL(fn_img)   # result: 50x50px (= `cliprect`) - expand has no effect on size
```

title: Pass width and height dimension in percents
description:
This comes from https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/2460 

In **knitr** we were using **webshot** but now default to **webshot2** is installed on the user side so that we can do screenshots of html widgets to include in PDF for example. Dimensions for the screenshot is passed from value set in chunk options `out.width` and `out.height` converted in `px` units, except if passed in % that we keep. This means for such chunk 

````markdown
```{r}
#| out.height="100%"
library(plotly)
p <- plot_ly(economics, x = ~date, y = ~unemploy / pop)
p
```
````

this will be equivalent to passing `vwidth = 468` and `vheight = "100%`. 

Simulating that outside of **knitr** we get the error also

````
> webshot2::webshot("https://github.com/rstudio/shiny", vwidth = 468, vheight = "100%")
Error in s$close() : attempt to apply non-function
````

<details>
<summary>Full backtrace </summary>

````
<error/rlang_error>
Error in `s$close()`:
! attempt to apply non-function
---
Backtrace:
     ▆
  1. └─webshot2::webshot(...)
  2.   └─cm$wait_for(p)
  3.     └─chromote:::synchronize(p, loop = private$child_loop)
  4.       ├─promises::with_promise_domain(...)
  5.       │ └─domain$wrapSync(expr)
  6.       │   └─base::force(expr)
  7.       └─base::tryCatch(...)
  8.         └─base (local) tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
  9.           └─base (local) tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
 10.             └─base (local) doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
````
</details>

I don't know if this is a **chromote** error only, or a **webshot2** one 

Or maybe `v(height|width)` can't be set in `%` - but if this is the case, then it could be checked early and error more friendly. We would also need to decide what to pass as value from **knitr**. 

Precision on why I consider this a potential error in **webshot2** - It was working with **webshot** 

````r
res <- webshot::webshot("https://github.com/rstudio/shiny", vwidth = 468, vheight = "100%")
str(res)
#> 'webshot' chr "webshot.png"
````

title: Errors received when using webshot2 (timeout and callback)
description:
I run _webshot2_ (v 0.1.0) on hundreds of images that I generate and I store the output in my hard disk, a few times per day. Some days it runs fine, but other days it stops with the following message: **Error: Chromote: timed out waiting for event Page.loadEventFired**. 

Thinking that it would be solved by increasing the delay, I changed it from 1 to 2, yesterday. However, today, after running successfully some 300 times, I received a new error message: **Error in deregister_callback_fn(): could not find function "deregister_callback_fn"**. I include both tracebacks below. I cannot reproduce the event that creates the errors (I ran _webshot2_ 10,000 times yesterday and it didn't issue any of the two errors. I include the code below, too.)

title: Enhancement:  Provide web debugging support
description:
The `rgl` package had [an issue](https://github.com/dmurdoch/rgl/issues/197) reported that I could only manage to replicate within a `webshot()` call.  It was a problem in the `rgl` Javascript code, so I needed to run the browser debugger to diagnose and fix it.  It took a while to figure out how to invoke the debugger, so I thought a nice enhancement would be to make this easier (e.g. a new argument to `webshot()` that made it do what I did).

Or, if this is too obscure, writing this issue will at least record the steps in case anyone else needs to do this.

Here are the details:

This location:  https://github.com/rstudio/webshot2/blob/6cc8950c43f992e5ed325410e9ade17f86aecde9/R/webshot.R#L258 is where the browser is told to navigate to the page where it's taking a snapshot.  If you run this command after that:
```
s$view()
```
it will open a browser window showing the browser debugger.  

The browser window only stays open as long as the `delay` that was requested in the call to `webshot()`, so you should set `delay = 300` or some other large number to give you enough time to make some debugging progress.

title: Should have a way to screenshot DOM elements to PDF
description:
Currently it's only possible to print an entire web page to standard paper size PDFs. The strategy used by puppeteer could be used to generate PDFs of specific DOM elements:
https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/puppeteer-examples/blob/master/element-to-pdf.js

title: Should add a max_concurrent parameter
description: It would be good to have a `max_concurrent` parameter, so that the user can provide a big list of URLs to screenshot and not have to worry about overloading their computer.

title: Support authenticated sites
description:
`webshot()` should support screenshots of authenticated sites. A potential workflow could follow the pattern of `token_fetch()` from the [gargle package](https://github.com/r-lib/gargle):

1. `webshot("auth.website.url")` detects that there’s an authentication layer in place (not sure if this is possible, but most auth sites will redirect to a login page if credentials are missing, so maybe check for that re-direct)
2. Offers to cache cookies
3. Opens a browser for the user to perform sign-in
4. Captures and optionally caches cookies
5. Continues on with capturing the screenshot

It may also be helpful to provide a `cookies` argument to `webshot()` so that authenticated sites can be accessed programmatically.

title: Chrome debugging port error with repeated attempts
description:
```r
for(i in 1:30){
    Sys.sleep(.1)
    webshot2::webshot("https://github.com/rstudio/webshot2",
                      file = glue::glue('{i}.png'),
                      delay = 0)
}
```

The code above takes 30 screenshots of this repository and saves it. As the loop starts working, it fails at an arbitrary iteration with the error 

```
Error in launch_chrome(path, args) : 
  Chrome debugging port not open after 10 seconds.
```

The `Sys.sleep` was added to possibly solve the issue but did not seem to help. I have experimented with as high as 2. It will fail regardless after a varying number of successful iterations.

The original use case is for creating a gif of the page with animation by incrementing the delay argument (unexpectedly works quite well apart from the error by the way. wouldn't expect the delay to be very precise)

Ubuntu 16.04
Chrome 72.0.3626.121
R 3.6
